subject: Mid-cycle capacity top-up: credit structure and priority banding options
messages:
From: Jason Liu <jason@cloudifylabs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.legal@cloudifylabs.com>, procurement@cloudifylabs.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Growing mid-year — options for adding capacity and priority lane

Hi Tessa,

Hope you’re well. We’re seeing product usage accelerate faster than forecasted and need to add roughly 40% more inference capacity for the remainder of our contract year. Two questions:

1) Can we add committed capacity mid-cycle and have it prorated to our existing term?
2) We’d like to buy a higher-priority execution tier for some critical API routes — can that be purchased as a separate add-on or does it require moving to a higher SKU?

We’re working on procurement timelines but wanted to understand commercial options (price, credits, lead time). I’ve attached the current SOW so you can see baseline capacity.

Thanks,
Jason
Director of Platform Engineering
Cloudify Labs
[Attachment: Cloudify_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Liu <jason@cloudifylabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Growing mid-year — options for adding capacity and priority lane

Hi Jason — thanks for the note and the SOW. Congrats on the growth — good problem to have. High level options that usually work for customers in this situation:

Option A — Pro-rated add-on (fastest):
- Add 40% committed capacity for the rest of the term, pro-rated by remaining months.
- One-time onboarding fee waived for add-ons under $75k.
- No change to priority tier; calls continue on existing pipeline.

Option B — Priority band + voucher (recommended if low-latency is critical):
- Purchase a "priority band" which reserves a portion of GPU pool for your critical routes.
- Priority band priced as a 6-month commitment (applied as a credit over remaining term) — effectively a staged voucher that reduces the pro-rate impact.
- Includes a 5% unit discount when combined with a top-up >30%.

Option C — Temporary burst + annualize: 
- Short-term burst capacity for 30 days at a premium, then convert to committed capacity at renewal with partial credit for burst spend.

Next steps I recommend: if you need quick capacity, Option A gets you live in 48 hours. If you want predictable latency and lower unit cost, Option B usually gives the best blended economics and priority guarantees.

I’m looping in Ben for a quick sketch of numbers and Monica for SOW changes. Can you share the internal target date for going live with the extra capacity?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-10T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Growing mid-year — options for adding capacity and priority lane

Quick numbers for the three options (illustrative):

- Current committed units: 1,000 RU/month (RU = Redwood units)
- Requested add: 400 RU/month (40% increase)
- Remaining term: 7 months

Option A (pro-rate):
- 400 RU * 7 months = 2,800 RU one-time top-up payment at your current unit price ($0.045/RU) => ~$126,000 pro-rated charge.

Option B (priority band + voucher):
- Priority band: reserve 150 RU at priority lane for 6 months = priced at $0.055/RU but applied as a voucher credit amortized over remaining 7 months.
- Voucher/credit applied: $20,000 credit spread across invoice schedule.
- Net blended unit price for the added RU after credit: ~ $0.037–0.041/RU depending on final band size.

Option C (burst then annualize):
- 30-day burst at $0.065/RU for 400 RU/month equivalent = ~$7,800 for the month. If converted to committed at renewal, 50% of burst spend converts to credit toward annual commit.

Notes and constraints:
- Legal will want an amendment to the SOW for Options B/C.
- For Option B the priority band requires a 14-day provisioning lead time.
- We can short-circuit procurement by issuing a one-off invoice for Option A and then amend at renewal.

Attaching a formalized price sheet for your procurement team.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Emily Park <emily.legal@cloudifylabs.com>

Date: 2027-05-12T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Growing mid-year — options for adding capacity and priority lane

Thanks for the options. Two procurement questions from legal/ops:

1) If we choose Option B, will Redwood provide a single amendment (SOW + order form) that includes the voucher credit language and the priority band SLA? We need the amendment for sign-off.
2) Can you confirm how credits will appear on invoices (line-item credit vs. netted-off price)? Our finance team requires explicit credit line items for audit.

Assuming both are feasible, Cloudify prefers Option B but needs the amendment and the invoice treatment confirmed to proceed. Target go-live: 2027-06-01.

Emily Park
Head of Legal Operations, Cloudify Labs
